questions.q: The correct order in aqueous medium of basic strength in case of methyl substituted amines is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In aqueous medium basic strength is dependent on electron density on nitrogen as well as solvation of cation formed after accepting H+. In protic solvent like water, the order of basic strength is

Me2NH>MeNH2>Me3N>NH3.

This happens beacuse in case of Me2NH there will be optimum (+I) and solvation while in MeNH2 has more significant hydration than Me3N.

questions.q: The final product A, formed in the following multistep reaction sequence is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Bromobenzene reacts with magnesium in dry ether (diethyl ether) to form phenylmagnesium bromide, often abbreviated as PhMgBr.

The resulting phenylmagnesium bromide reacts with carbon dioxide in the presence of an acidic medium to form benzoic acid.

Heating benzoic acid with ammonia can lead to a reaction known as the Schotten-Baumann type reaction, which is a method for the amidation of carboxylic acids. In this reaction, the carboxylic acid group of benzoic acid reacts with ammonia  to form an amide, benzamide, under heating conditions.

When an amide is treated with bromine in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide, degradation of amide takes place leading to the formation of primary amine.

In this case, it is an hoffmann bromamide reaction, aniline is formed.

questions.q: A compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> with molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>108</mn><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> undergoes acetylation to give product with molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>192</mn><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The number of amino groups in the compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> is ________.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The compounds like amines and alcohols undergo acetylation with acetyl chloride. During this reaction, one proton of amine or alcohol is replaced with one acetyl group(CH3CO-).

The molar mass of the acetyl group is 43 g/mol. The increase in molar mass due to one acetyl group is 43-1=42g/mol.

The molar mass of reactant is 108 g/mol. The molar mass of product is 192 g/mol.  The change in mass is 84.

Hence, the number of acetyl groups =8442=2
